title: Erdős #550: Ramsey Numbers for Trees and Multipartite Graphs
description: For T a tree on n vertices and G = K_{m₁,...,mₖ}, prove R(T,G) ≤ (χ(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})-1)+m₁. Chvátal (1977): R(T,Kₘ) = (m-1)(n-1)+1 is the foundational result.

meta.author: Paul Erdős, Václav Chvátal
meta.assumptions: 5 axioms: ramsey_exists, chvatal, erdos_conjecture_open, bipartite_case, burr_conjecture. See Lean source for complete statements.

overview.historicalContext:
**Chvátal's Breakthrough (1977)**

Václav Chvátal proved one of the most elegant exact results in Ramsey theory: R(T, Kₘ) = (m-1)(n-1) + 1 for ANY tree T on n vertices. Unlike most Ramsey numbers which have only asymptotic bounds, this gives an exact closed formula. The proof uses a beautiful induction on tree structure.

**Erdős's Generalization**

Erdős asked (Problem #550, circa 1985): can Chvátal's result extend to complete multipartite graphs? If G = K_{m₁,...,mₖ}, he conjectured R(T,G) ≤ (χ(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})-1) + m₁. This bound is recursive—it uses the bipartite Ramsey number as a building block.

**The Problem's Status**

Despite partial progress on special cases (bounded-degree trees, paths, stars), the general conjecture remains OPEN. The difficulty lies in handling arbitrary multipartite structures beyond the bipartite case.

**Related Results**

Burr's conjecture (now proved) established linear bounds R(T, K₃) ≤ C·n for bounded-degree trees. The Gerencsér-Gyárfás theorem gives exact path-vs-path Ramsey numbers. These special cases inform but don't resolve the general problem.
overview.problemStatement: Let m₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ mₖ and n be sufficiently large. If T is a tree on n vertices and G is the complete multipartite graph K_{m₁,...,mₖ}, prove that R(T,G) ≤ (χ(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})-1)+m₁.
overview.text: For T a tree on n vertices and G = K_{m₁,...,mₖ}, prove R(T,G) ≤ (χ(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})-1)+m₁. Chvátal (1977): R(T,Kₘ) = (m-1)(n-1)+1 is the foundational result.
overview.proofStrategy: We formalize trees, complete multipartite graphs, Ramsey numbers, Chvátal's theorem, the main conjecture, special cases (paths, stars, bounded degree), probabilistic lower bounds, extremal constructions, and asymptotic behavior.
keyInsights: The bound reduces to Chvátal when G = Kₘ
Burr's conjecture for bounded-degree trees is proved
For fixed m, R(T_n, Kₘ) ~ (m-1)n asymptotically

sections.title: Part I: Basic Graph Definitions
sections.summary: IsTree (connected and acyclic) and vertexCount (Fintype.card V).
sections.mathContext: Tree: connected acyclic graph on $n$ vertices with $n-1$ edges.

sections.title: Part II: Complete Multipartite Graphs
sections.summary: CompleteMultipartite structure (k parts with sorted sizes m₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ mₖ), totalVertices, chromaticNumber = k, completeGraphAsMultipartite (Kₘ as m parts of size 1), completeBipartite K_{m₁,m₂}.

sections.title: Part III: Ramsey Numbers
sections.summary: ramsey_exists (axiom: a Ramsey N exists for any T and multipartite G) and ramseyNumber R(T, G) defined as Nat.find over that existence.
sections.mathContext: $R(T,G)$: least $N$ such that every 2-colouring of $K_N$ contains a red $T$ or a blue $G$.

sections.title: Part IV: Chvátal's Theorem
sections.summary: chvatal (axiom, 1977): R(T, Kₘ) = (m-1)(n-1) + 1 for any tree T on n vertices, plus four native_decide examples verifying the formula.
sections.mathContext: Chvátal (1977): $R(T,K_m) = (m-1)(n-1)+1$ for any tree $T$ on $n$ vertices.

sections.title: Part V: The Conjecture
sections.summary: ConjecturedBound ((χ-1)(R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})-1) + m₁), ErdosConjecture (the bound holds for all large trees and multipartite G), erdos_conjecture_open (axiom marking it OPEN).
sections.mathContext: Erdős's conjecture: $R(T,G) \leq (\chi(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m_1,m_2})-1) + m_1$, extending Chvátal to multipartite $G$.

sections.title: Part VI: Special Cases
sections.summary: complete_graph_case (reduces to Chvátal when G = Kₘ), bipartite_case (axiom bound for K_{m,m}), starGraph (K_{1,n-1}).
sections.mathContext: Known reductions: $G=K_m$ recovers Chvátal; bipartite $K_{m,m}$ and stars $K_{1,n-1}$ have explicit bounds.

sections.title: Part VII: Path Graphs
sections.summary: IsPath: a tree with maximum degree ≤ 2 and exactly two degree-1 endpoints (the path graph P_n).
sections.mathContext: Path $P_n$: a tree where every vertex has degree $\leq 2$ and two endpoints have degree $1$.

sections.title: Part VIII: General Tree Structure
sections.summary: maxDegree (sup of vertex degrees), BurrConjecture (linear Ramsey bound for bounded-degree trees), burr_conjecture (axiom: the conjecture holds).
sections.mathContext: Burr: for trees of bounded max degree $\Delta$, $R(T,K_3) = O(n)$ — linear in the number of vertices.

sections.title: Part IX: Turán-Type Connections
sections.summary: turanNumber: the Turán number ex(n, Kᵣ) = (1 - 1/(r-1)) n²/2, the maximum edge count of an n-vertex Kᵣ-free graph.
sections.mathContext: Turán: $\mathrm{ex}(n,K_r) = (1 - \tfrac{1}{r-1})\tfrac{n^2}{2}$, linking extremal edge counts to Ramsey bounds.

sections.title: Part X: Probabilistic Lower Bounds
sections.summary: Placeholder banner for probabilistic lower-bound constructions; no declarations yet in this file.
sections.mathContext: Probabilistic (random colouring) arguments give lower bounds on $R(T,G)$; not yet formalized here.

sections.title: Part XI: Extremal Graphs
sections.summary: RamseyExtremalGraph: the (m-1)(n-1)-vertex extremal construction (m-1 disjoint red cliques of size n-1) with no red tree and no blue Kₘ, witnessing the lower bound for Chvátal's formula.
sections.mathContext: Extremal witness: $(m-1)$ disjoint red $K_{n-1}$'s give $(m-1)(n-1)$ vertices with no red tree and no blue $K_m$.

sections.title: Part XII: Asymptotic Behavior
sections.summary: Placeholder banner for asymptotic behavior, followed by the closing file summary (status OPEN, the conjecture, known results, and key axioms: chvatal, erdos_conjecture_open, bipartite_case, burr_conjecture).
sections.mathContext: Open: precise asymptotics of $R(T,K_{m_1,\dots,m_k})$; Chvátal gives the exact complete-graph case, the multipartite extension remains conjectural.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures Erdős Problem #550 on Ramsey numbers for trees and complete multipartite graphs. The conjecture extends Chvátal's exact result R(T,Kₘ) = (m-1)(n-1)+1 to multipartite graphs using a recursive bound involving the chromatic number.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: The problem connects tree embedding with Ramsey theory.

Chvátal's theorem provides the complete answer for complete graphs, but the extension to multipartite graphs remains open. Special cases like bounded-degree trees (Burr's conjecture) have been resolved.
openQuestions: Does the conjectured bound hold for all sufficiently large n?
What is the exact value of R(T, K_{m,m}) for general trees?
Can the bound be improved for specific tree families?
What is the relationship to Turán extremal graphs?
